96:## What Are Claude Skills?
98:Claude Skills are reusable instruction packages that teach an AI agent how to handle a specific class of tasks. Each skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter (name, description) and Markdown instructions, optionally bundled with scripts, references, and assets. Anthropic introduced the format in October 2025 and released it as an [open standard](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) in December 2025; it's now supported by Claude Code, Claude.ai, the Claude API, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and Windsurf.
100:Skills load progressively. At session start, the agent sees only each skill's name and description — roughly 100 tokens per skill. The full SKILL.md body (typically under 5,000 tokens) loads only when the agent decides the skill is relevant to the current task. Auxiliary files in `scripts/` and `references/` load on demand. This is what lets a single agent host hundreds of skills without bloating its context window.
102:Skills are not MCP servers and not tools. MCP defines how an agent connects to external systems — auth, transport, tool discovery. Tools are the individual functions an agent invokes. Skills define the workflow — what to do, in what order, with what guardrails — once the agent has the connections and tools it needs. In production, all three layers run together: MCP for access, tools for actions, skills for behavior.

334:## Getting Started
336:### Using Skills in Claude.ai
338:1. Click the skill icon (🧩) in your chat interface.
339:2. Add skills from the marketplace or upload custom skills.
340:3. Claude automatically activates relevant skills based on your task.
342:### Using Skills in Claude Code
344:1. Place the skill in `~/.config/claude-code/skills/`:
346:   mkdir -p ~/.config/claude-code/skills/
347:   cp -r skill-name ~/.config/claude-code/skills/
350:2. Verify skill metadata:
352:   head ~/.config/claude-code/skills/skill-name/SKILL.md
355:3. Start Claude Code:
360:4. The skill loads automatically and activates when relevant.
362:### Using Skills via API
364:Use the Claude Skills API to programmatically load and manage skills:
373:    skills=["skill-id-here"],
378:See the [Skills API documentation](https://docs.claude.com/en/api/skills-guide) for details.
380:## Creating Skills
382:### Skill Structure
384:Each skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter:
387:skill-name/
394:### Basic Skill Template
398:name: my-skill-name
399:description: A clear description of what this skill does and when to use it.
402:# My Skill Name
404:Detailed description of the skill's purpose and capabilities.
406:## When to Use This Skill
412:## Instructions
414:[Detailed instructions for Claude on how to execute this skill]
416:## Examples
418:[Real-world examples showing the skill in action]
421:### Skill Best Practices
425:- Write instructions for Claude, not end users
426:- Test across Claude.ai, Claude Code, and API
430:## Contributing
434:- How to submit new skills
439:### Quick Contribution Steps

442:2. Check for duplicates in existing skills
443:3. Follow the skill structure template
444:4. Test your skill across platforms

307: - `STAGED` → `REJECTED-POST-PROBE`: axis-fail or Probe DAG REJECT
308: - `STAGED` → `DEFERRED-PENDING-FIX`: upstream issue blocks install; cite-only retained as substitute
309: - `INSTALLED-AMBER` → `INSTALLED`: deferred fix landed
310: - ANY → re-evaluation triggered per `docs/install-from-github-discipline.md §"When to re-install"`

312: ### `@latest` resolution at execute time (per Wave 50 fire 8 Pattern A on Agent I F-4 — operationalizes CR-9 version-pin mandate)
313: 
314: Every install command in this manifest tagged `@latest` (e.g., `npm install -g @doobidoo/mcp-memory-service@latest`, `docker pull qdrant/qdrant:latest`, `npm install -g markdownlint-cli2@latest`) carries **implicit `@latest-acknowledged-D6-risk:2026-05-06` status** — the manifest planning intent is "pull newest at install execution per CR-6, with explicit D6 today-release-auto-upgrade risk acknowledgment per CR-9". At install execution, the operator MUST:
315: 
316: 1. Resolve the actual version (e.g., `npm view @doobidoo/mcp-memory-service version` returns `1.4.7` → install command becomes `npm install -g @doobidoo/mcp-memory-service@1.4.7`)
317: 2. Record both the `@latest` planning intent AND the resolved `@<resolved-version>` in `docs/install-provenance.md` under the install row (per CR-6 D6 risk-acknowledged contract)
318: 3. Pin the manifest install command to the resolved version post-install (manifest row updated from `@latest` to `@<resolved-version>` as part of `STAGED → INSTALLED` promotion)
319: 4. Re-evaluation trigger: per `docs/install-from-github-discipline.md §"When to re-install"` — the resolved-version pin holds until either a re-install is needed (per upstream changelog or sibling D6 evidence) OR the row's manifest age exceeds N-day re-evaluation cadence
320: 
321: **Rationale**: the manifest's `@latest` install commands ARE the SOTA-discipline contract per CR-6 fresh-from-github (do not pre-pin to stale versions in the planning document). The resolution-at-execute-time + provenance-recording gate satisfies CR-9 version-pin mandate without violating CR-6 fresh-from-github. The promotion-gate state machine above enforces this — a row cannot advance `STAGED → INSTALLED` until step 3 (resolved-version pin) lands in the manifest row.
322: 
323: **Scope**: applies to ALL install commands carrying raw `@latest` AND `@HEAD`-equivalent pulls (`git clone --depth 1 ... origin/main` without SHA pin). Does NOT apply to `@<version-tag>` pinned install commands (those satisfy CR-9 directly).

606:    - probe upstream repo + alternative repos via mcp__github__search_repositories (axis-1 maintainership filter)
607:    - probe CCBP cite anchors at Z:/repos/deps/claude-code-best-practice-shan/
608:    - probe Wave 47 GRAND CATALOG at Z:/claude-sota/tmp/wave47-grand-catalog-2026-05-06.md (934 repos / 125 perfect-convergence baseline)
609:    - probe sibling claude-sota memory entries at Z:/claude-sota/.claude/projects/Z--claude-sota/memory/ for prior-decisions
610: 3. CLASSIFY return per cardinal-rule-10 priority order:
611:    (a) Install canonical SOTA solution → execute install per Pattern 1-6
612:    (b) Cite-adapt SOTA pattern → cite-anchor + adapt with cardinal-rule-8 conformance
613:    (c) Best SOTA-recommended approach → operator gate + axis-1+2+3 verdict
614:    (d) HONEST-NON-FINDING → escalate to operator
615: 4. LOG to install-provenance.md with research provenance (sota-researcher invocation + return + classification + decision)
616: ```

96: ## What Are Claude Skills?
97: 
98: Claude Skills are reusable instruction packages that teach an AI agent how to handle a specific class of tasks. Each skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter (name, description) and Markdown instructions, optionally bundled with scripts, references, and assets. Anthropic introduced the format in October 2025 and released it as an [open standard](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) in December 2025; it's now supported by Claude Code, Claude.ai, the Claude API, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and Windsurf.
99: 
100: Skills load progressively. At session start, the agent sees only each skill's name and description — roughly 100 tokens per skill. The full SKILL.md body (typically under 5,000 tokens) loads only when the agent decides the skill is relevant to the current task. Auxiliary files in `scripts/` and `references/` load on demand. This is what lets a single agent host hundreds of skills without bloating its context window.
101: 
102: Skills are not MCP servers and not tools. MCP defines how an agent connects to external systems — auth, transport, tool discovery. Tools are the individual functions an agent invokes. Skills define the workflow — what to do, in what order, with what guardrails — once the agent has the connections and tools it needs. In production, all three layers run together: MCP for access, tools for actions, skills for behavior.
103:

334: ## Getting Started
335: 
336: ### Using Skills in Claude.ai
337: 
338: 1. Click the skill icon (🧩) in your chat interface.
339: 2. Add skills from the marketplace or upload custom skills.
340: 3. Claude automatically activates relevant skills based on your task.
341: 
342: ### Using Skills in Claude Code
343: 
344: 1. Place the skill in `~/.config/claude-code/skills/`:
345:    ```bash
346:    mkdir -p ~/.config/claude-code/skills/
347:    cp -r skill-name ~/.config/claude-code/skills/
348:    ```
349: 
350: 2. Verify skill metadata:
351:    ```bash
352:    head ~/.config/claude-code/skills/skill-name/SKILL.md
353:    ```
354: 
355: 3. Start Claude Code:
356:    ```bash
357:    claude
358:    ```
359: 
360: 4. The skill loads automatically and activates when relevant.
361: 
362: ### Using Skills via API
363: 
364: Use the Claude Skills API to programmatically load and manage skills:
365: 
366: ```python
367: import anthropic
368: 
369: client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key="your-api-key")
370: 
371: response = client.messages.create(
372:     model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",
373:     skills=["skill-id-here"],
374:     messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Your prompt"}]
375: )
376: ```
377: 
378: See the [Skills API documentation](https://docs.claude.com/en/api/skills-guide) for details.
379: 
380: ## Creating Skills
381: 
382: ### Skill Structure
383: 
384: Each skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter:
385: 
386: ```
387: skill-name/
388: ├── SKILL.md          # Required: Skill instructions and metadata
389: ├── scripts/          # Optional: Helper scripts
390: ├── templates/        # Optional: Document templates
391: └── resources/        # Optional: Reference files
392: ```
393: 
394: ### Basic Skill Template
395: 
396: ```markdown
397: ---
398: name: my-skill-name
399: description: A clear description of what this skill does and when to use it.
400: ---
401: 
402: # My Skill Name
403: 
404: Detailed description of the skill's purpose and capabilities.
405: 
406: ## When to Use This Skill
407: 
408: - Use case 1
409: - Use case 2
410: - Use case 3
411: 
412: ## Instructions
413: 
414: [Detailed instructions for Claude on how to execute this skill]
415: 
416: ## Examples
417: 
418: [Real-world examples showing the skill in action]
419: ```
420: 
421: ### Skill Best Practices
422: 
423: - Focus on specific, repeatable tasks
424: - Include clear examples and edge cases
425: - Write instructions for Claude, not end users
426: - Test across Claude.ai, Claude Code, and API
427: - Document prerequisites and dependencies
428: - Include error handling guidance
429: 
430: ## Contributing
431: 
432: We welcome contributions! Please read our [Contributing Guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md) for details on:
